title: Doc-Type Filter Hides the Recovery Bulletin
summary: An operator asks how to restart a sensor array after a coolant fault. The right procedure exists in the corpus, but a doc-type filter only allows FAQs, so the recovery bulletin never enters the packed context.
query: What must operators do before restarting the ArcLight sensor array after a coolant fault?

dataset.name: ArcLight incident-response packet
dataset.notes: Synthetic engineering-operations corpus with a recovery bulletin, FAQ, incident digest, checklist, and maintenance memo.

debugChecklist: If the surviving answer sounds operationally thin, inspect whether the system filtered to lightweight document classes like FAQs.
Check whether the excluded documents contain prescriptive language such as must, required, or before restart.
When the issue is doc-type filtering, fix the candidate policy before tweaking ranking or prompts.

chunks.label: Bulletin chunk 1
chunks.text: Before any restart after a coolant fault, operators must complete a dry-spin validation of the turbine cage and record the resulting vibration trace.

chunks.label: Bulletin chunk 2
chunks.text: The restart request also requires a thermal lead sign-off confirming that coolant pressure has stabilized and the dry-spin trace stayed within tolerance.

chunks.label: FAQ chunk 1
chunks.text: After a coolant fault, inspect the loop, clear the controller warning, and restart once the dashboard returns to normal.

chunks.label: Digest chunk 1
chunks.text: Recent ArcLight faults were traced to insufficient verification of the turbine cage after coolant loss.

chunks.label: Checklist chunk 1
chunks.text: Do not restart any array with an unresolved coolant alarm. Escalate to the thermal lead when vibration behavior looks unusual.

chunks.label: Memo chunk 1
chunks.text: Older practice allowed restart after dashboard normalization alone, but the 2025 bulletin added dry-spin verification and thermal sign-off.

runs.outcome: The answer restarts too early and misses the two mandatory safeguards.
